name: Cable Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
summary: A vertical pulling exercise performed on a cable station using parallel handles to target the lats with reduced shoulder strain.

setup: Attach a neutral-grip handle or parallel-grip bar to the high pulley of a lat pulldown station.
Adjust the thigh pad so your legs are firmly secured with feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with palms facing each other, sit down, and anchor your thighs beneath the pads with arms fully extended overhead.
steps: Depress your scapulae and pull the handle downward toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Pause briefly at the bottom as the handle approaches collarbone level, maintaining an upright torso with a slight backward lean.
Control the weight as you smoothly extend your arms back overhead, allowing your shoulder blades to upwardly rotate into a full stretch.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as your arms extend overhead, and exhale as you pull the handles down toward your chest.
cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Pull your shoulder blades down into your back pockets.
Keep your chest lifted toward the cable.

common_faults.fault: Excessive backward swinging of the torso to use momentum.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a steady, slight lean back throughout the movement without rocking at the hips.

common_faults.fault: Pulling primarily through the forearms and biceps without engaging the back.
common_faults.correction: Initiate the movement by depressing the shoulder blades and driving your elbows down toward your hips.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the top range of motion short.
common_faults.correction: Allow your arms to fully straighten and your lats to stretch at the top of each rep.

precautions: Ensure the thigh support is locked securely to keep you anchored to the seat under heavy loads.
Do not pull the handle behind your neck.
